claims.claim: Two strippers exist with DISJOINT token sets, which is why one-lever fixes kept missing. extractQualifiers() inside parseIngredientLine() removes tokens in QUALIFIERS (raw/dried/canned/whole) before normalizeIngredientName() sees them — proof by the one input where the two disagree: parseIngredientLine('dried apricots').name is 'apricots' while normalizeIngredientName('dried apricots').cleaned is 'dried apricots'. But the cooking verbs (grilled/scrambled/steamed/...) are ABSENT from QUALIFIERS, so for them the prep_phrases strip is the only one and is fully load-bearing. CORRECTS the pre-2026-08-01 reading that editing prep_phrases is a no-op: that holds only for the QUALIFIERS tokens.

Paired guard. The cooking verbs stay OUT of prep_phrases AND RULES_VERSION stays >= 2. claims.claim: buildFatSecretResult's counted-request fallback scans for a serving whose label word is a word of the REQUEST, via count-label.ts's labelPieceMatchesItem, not only the request's last token. Both jest projects load jest.setup.no-llm.js via setupFiles, so no test can reach a live LLM provider. Five mapper modules import 'dotenv/config' at module scope, so before this a test importing the mapper chain held the developer's real keys -- measured 129 billable OpenRouter round trips over 10 runs of one suite. The second half of the command is the load-bearing one: the gate must ASSIGN '' and must never `delete process.env.X`, because dotenv only writes a key it does not already own, so a delete hands the real key straight back and the gate looks identical while doing nothing. CI has no key and was green throughout, so CI is not a check on this.

A flavour word must not become a distinct ingredient. data/fatsecret/normalization-rules.json carried an unguarded synonym_rewrites entry vanilla -> vanilla extract which fired before any LLM ran, so `vanilla yogurt` was searched as `vanilla extract yogurt` and resolved to a 288 kcal/100g, 4.2 g ingredient (MEASURED cold on the live box 2026-08-03; `vanilla protein shake` billed 150 g = 429 kcal of extract). DEFAULT_RULES never held that entry and the in-code rule implementing the same recipe default IS context-gated on a following food noun, but readRulesFile() prefers the on-disk JSON so the naive entry won. Asserts BOTH halves: the flavour-plus-food form is left alone AND bare vanilla still gets the intended recipe default. Output is normalize(vanilla yogurt)|normalize(vanilla).

THE DELIVERED HALF of the flavour-promotion fix, and the only check that can see it. data/ is in the box's .stignore so Syncthing NEVER carries data/fatsecret/normalization-rules.json to /home/owner/Recipe-App, and readRulesFile() prefers that on-disk JSON over DEFAULT_RULES. A stale copy therefore reinstates vanilla -> vanilla extract on the LIVE service while every Mac-side gate stays green, including the backend-context twin vanilla-rewrite-is-context-gated, which reads the Mac file. Same failure shape as PR #211, which sat inert on the box until an scp on 2026-08-01. Output is bareVanillaRewriteCount@synonymRewriteCount: a missing, unreadable or unparseable file emits nothing and FAILS, never passes.

The model may UPGRADE the branded-query flag and may downgrade it only where the static brand evidence is decisive. mapIngredientWithFallback() seeds isBrandedQuery from detectBrandInQuery() and then overwrites it at TWO sites - the live LLM branch and the normalize-gate-skipped branch that replays AiNormalizeCache.isBranded. Both were plain assignments, so a model answering false vetoed the static detector, suppressing the brand-targeted supplementary OFF query in gatherCandidates(), the brand_guard escape, the canReuseQuickGather brand re-search, and the +4 admission bonus in computeOffScore(). This guards the WIRING, which is the failure that recurs here (#221, #223, #226 were each a correct rule with a caller that never used it, and #230's own predicate test passed while an earlier draft sat at the wrong layer). Plain upgrade-only is REFUTED: 42 of 56 downgrades are the model correcting a lexicon false positive and carry 292 of the population's 310 reads. Output is resolverCallSites@rawOverwritesRemaining.

The normalize-gate SKIP rate over the box's [AI:*] tag stream is in the 50s-60s percent (60% measured 2026-08-05: 11,932 GATE vs 7,928 NORM over 122 files; it read 56% on 2026-08-04). This is a property of the accumulated LOG CORPUS, not of the system, and it drifts upward with eval activity - seven cold golden runs moved it 56 -> 60 with no code change, so the band is deliberately wide and a move inside it is not a signal. The `-h` on grep is load-bearing - without it `grep -o` over a multi-file glob prefixes each match with its filename and a per-file count reads as the corpus, which is how a 74.9% figure once got documented here. Counting the bare tag body rather than the whole [AI:...] token keeps combined tags like [AI:GATE+SERV] counted once.
claims.command: cd /home/owner/Recipe-App/logs && g=$(grep -oh "AI:GATE" mapping-summary-*.txt | wc -l) && n=$(grep -oh "AI:NORM" mapping-summary-*.txt | wc -l) && echo $(( g * 100 / (g + n) ))

claims.claim: SERVING_AI_TIERS excludes ai_generated_serving. The tier names are unreliable in BOTH directions: getAiServingGrams() runs no model despite the name, while fdc_size_estimate (the largest maybeCalled serving tier) has no 'ai' in its name. A substring rule on 'ai' gets both wrong, so the table must stay an explicit allowlist. Membership means maybeCalled -- an UPPER BOUND on model calls, measured 2.6x overstatement 2026-08-05 (owner: mobile sync-docs/reports/2026-08-05_ai-serving-spend-audit.md section 3); the earlier registry text's 'getOrCreateFdcSizeServings() has no cache' stayed true, but the inference from it (every event a live LLM round trip) is REFUTED -- 41 fdc_size_* events, 0 model responses.

simpleRerank abstention (the `if (!winner)` block in mapIngredientWithFallback()) has TWO labelled exits, not one: confidence_gate_backstop when confidenceGate() had a pick, scored_by_confidence otherwise — plus a third leg below MIN_FALLBACK_CONFIDENCE that writes no selectionReason at all. Counting abstention by grepping confidence_gate_backstop alone undercounts it ~10x (15 vs 159 on the post-cee10fd corpus), which is exactly how the autonomous brief's original W1 decision rule would have closed a live population. This claim reddens if a leg is added or renamed, which is the prompt to re-measure the population in the owner doc.

The mapping-analysis corpus records topCandidates = filtered.slice(0, 5) in GATHER order, while simpleRerank actually scores buildRerankPool(filtered, RERANK_POOL_LIMIT) with RERANK_POOL_LIMIT = 10. Any pool size read from mapping-analysis-*.json is therefore a LOWER BOUND, and scored[0] cannot be reconstructed offline unless the slice returned fewer than 5 (which proves filtered fit inside the window). Measured 2026-08-04: this makes 124 of the 159 post-cee10fd abstentions unmeasurable read-only, and an offline reconstruction that ignores the truncation validates at 43.0% against 98.6% on determined pools. Value is <log-site count>@<pool limit>; it reddens if either side of the asymmetry moves.

hydrateAndSelectServing()'s stale-cache branch deletes a cached size serving when the resolved weight exceeds maxAIGrams. Its fdc_/off_ deleteMany calls MUST filter on isAiEstimated:true. targetSizeUnit is exactly 'small'|'medium'|'large', which is the same key space USDA's own size servings occupy: 94 of the 109 exact-name size rows in FdcServing are genuine source='usda_fdc'/isAiEstimated=false against 15 ai/true (measured 2026-08-04). Unfiltered, the branch destroys curated USDA data, and it fires precisely on foods that are legitimately heavy -- a genuine 'medium' cabbage head at 588g trips the 500g ceiling and is deleted for being correct. SCOPE, read this first: where=backend means cwd is the Syncthing'd copy of the Mac's WORKING TREE, so this greps a code shape SOMEBODY HAS CHECKED OUT -- not master, not the served .next (CLAUDE.md Doc rules, the 25-of-100 fail-open class). It can be green on the box's nightly while the guard is unmerged and undeployed. For 'is it LIVE', use the sibling box claim fs-ambiguous-persist-guard-premise-holds plus the deploy falsifier in the owner doc (grep the served chunk under /home/owner/Recipe-App/.next/server/). FOUR guards, a@b@c@d, and the command strips comments first so a breadcrumb comment can never satisfy one -- the previous version matched 'catch (error) { ... ambiguous_backfill.save_failed' anywhere in the file, which stayed GREEN when the warn was downgraded to logger.debug and when the warn was deleted and replaced by a comment naming it (both mutations run 2026-08-05). (d) findExistingServing() short-circuits symmetrically, and (d) is ANCHORED TO THAT FUNCTION'S SIGNATURE -- the first cut was the bare literal 'if (!hasServingWriteTarget(foodId)) return null;', which stayed green when the read guard was deleted from findExistingServing() and the identical line added to borrowSiblingServing() (mutation run 2026-08-05). Why any of this: AiGeneratedServing.foodId is a FK to AiGeneratedFood.id and no fs_ row exists there, so every FatSecret ambiguous estimate raised AiGeneratedServing_foodId_fkey -- 338 save_failed lines box-wide of which 311 are fs_, over 61 foods and 167 food+unit pairs, measured 2026-08-05 (next-start.log is append-only, so quote the date and prefer the two stable counts). Do NOT convert this into a write target: FatSecretServing has no source/isAiEstimated/confidence/note column (the attribution boundary in CLAUDE.md) and fsHasServingShape() is a findFirst on grams>0 with no provenance filter, so a synthetic row flips 5 records SHAPELESS->SHAPED at the save gate (6 of the 61 are shapeless; 5 have a FatSecretFood parent so the write would land, and fs_86607832 has none and would still throw) -- 5 measured, not the 3,472 corpus-wide #16 ceiling it was confused with.
claims.command: node -e "const src=require('fs').readFileSync('src/lib/mapping/ambiguous-unit-backfill.ts','utf8');const s=src.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g,'').replace(/(^|[^:])\/\/[^\n]*/gm,(_m,p)=>p);const a=/if \(!hasServingWriteTarget\(foodId\)\) \{\s*logger\.warn\('ambiguous_backfill\.persist_skipped_no_target'[\s\S]{0,200}?return false;/.test(s)?1:0;const b=/await upsertServing\(foodId, normalizedUnit, result\.estimatedGrams[\s\S]{0,400}?\} catch \(error\) \{\s*logger\.warn\('ambiguous_backfill\.save_failed'/.test(s)?1:0;const c=/if \(persisted\) \{\s*logger\.info\('ambiguous_backfill\.saved'/.test(s)?1:0;const d=/async function findExistingServing\(foodId: string, normalizedUnit: string\) \{\s*if \(!hasServingWriteTarget\(foodId\)\) return null;/.test(s)?1:0;process.stdout.write(a+'@'+b+'@'+c+'@'+d)"

claims.claim: The Phase 0.5(c) billed-response counter fires in makeRequest() the moment the envelope has been read, and BEFORE the rawContent guard. That ordering is the whole item: makeRequest() returns success:false for FOUR separate shapes of billed 2xx -- an envelope that fails response.json(), an empty choices array, content that fails JSON.parse, and an error field inside the model's own JSON -- so a counter placed in callStructuredLlm()'s success branch would rebuild exactly the structural undercount 0.5(c) exists to close. SEMANTICS, and they are the reason this claim was re-cut: `responses` is EXACT, not a floor. makeRequest() counts exactly one outcome per HTTP attempt (countResponse / countFailure), so responses + failures === attempts. The first cut made it a LOWER BOUND -- response.json() threw into the outer catch, so a billed 2xx with an unreadable envelope incremented only failures. That shape now increments responses and unparseableEnvelopes. Token and cost sums remain FLOORS, read against usageReported / costReported. The command asserts the source order response.json() < countResponse() < rawContent-guard; it prints 'bad' on master @ 136d0e5 (verified 2026-08-04), so it is a real check and not a tautology. Mutation-proved by structured-client-usage-capture.test.ts > '200 with empty choices is counted as a billed response' and > 'a 200 whose envelope will not parse is still counted as a billed response'.
claims.command: awk '/await response.json\(\)/{if(!p)p=NR} /countResponse\(/{if(p&&!r)r=NR} /const rawContent = payload/{if(!c)c=NR} END{print (p>0 && r>p && c>r) ? "ok" : "bad"}' src/lib/ai/structured-client.ts

claims.claim: Every usage-counter call in structured-client.ts goes through countSafely(), so a throw from telemetry can never change the outcome of the request it measures. This is the fail-open instrument class INVERTED: the counters sit inside code the request's own error handling owns, so an unguarded throw from recordLlmResponse() would land in makeRequest()'s catch and turn an ALREADY BILLED, usable LLM answer into success:false and then into a retry that bills again, while an unguarded throw from recordLlmLogicalSuccess() would reject the caller's promise outright -- nothing catches around that call site. The command reads '<all recordLlm*({ call sites>@<those wrapped in countSafely>' with whitespace stripped (the file is CRLF, so \r must be stripped too or the multi-line call reads as unwrapped); 3@3 here, 0@0 on master @ 136d0e5 which has no counters. A new counter call added raw moves the left number only. Mutation-proved by structured-client-telemetry-cannot-fail-the-call.test.ts: replacing countSafely()'s body with a bare record() call kills 3 of its 4 tests (measured 2026-08-04).
claims.command: echo "$(tr -d ' \t\r\n' < src/lib/ai/structured-client.ts | grep -o 'recordLlm[A-Za-z]*({' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')@$(tr -d ' \t\r\n' < src/lib/ai/structured-client.ts | grep -o 'countSafely(()=>recordLlm[A-Za-z]*({' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"

claims.claim: The two simpleRerank-abstention legs never report a raw retrieval score, and they do it in TWO DIFFERENT WAYS because only one of them is safe to overwrite. Site A is the scored_by_confidence arm of the `if (!winner)` block in mapIngredientWithFallback(); it used to write `confidence = winner.score`, which is a cross-source, unbounded retrieval score (computeOffScore median 6.900 on this population) and saturated to a cached 1.000 at the clamp downstream -- a decision the reranker REFUSED to make, stored as maximally confident. It now ASSIGNS the named constant RERANK_DECLINED_CONFIDENCE, which is safe there because the arm is gated on `score >= 0.80 AND assessConfidence >= 0.60`, so it has a floor. Site B is confidenceGate()'s basic_produce_bypass exit in gather-candidates.ts, which returned Math.max(0, Math.min(1, top1.score)); confidence_gate_backstop reads gateResult.confidence with no reason scope, so that clamp was the same laundering one layer up. Site B has NO score floor, so it takes the constant as a CEILING -- Math.min(RERANK_DECLINED_CONFIDENCE, Math.max(0, Math.min(1, top1.score))) -- and NOT as a flat assignment. That distinction is the whole point of term 3 and is measured, not stylistic: of 295 basic_produce_bypass decisions in the box's 111 mapping-analysis-*.json (2026-08-05), 288 sit at a saturated 1.000, 1 at 0.810, and 6 at 0.67551, and 0.67551 is below SUB_THRESHOLD_SAVE_FLOOR (0.75). A flat 0.78 would therefore RAISE those 6 into cacheable range -- a loosening inside a PR whose thesis is that refused decisions must stop being cached as confident. CACHEABILITY IS THE WHOLE JUSTIFICATION; an earlier version of this text also said the badge lifts from low to medium and that was FALSE, verified 2026-08-05 in the mobile repo: CONFIDENCE_LEVELS.medium.min is 0.5 and getConfidenceLevel() compares >=, so 0.67551 and 0.78 both render medium 'Good Estimate' (false under this repo's own confidence >= 0.6 ? 'medium' mapping too). It mattered because this command does not test the badge assertion, so the nightly would have reported the sentence green indefinitely -- doc rules 1 and 2. The four output terms are declined@raw@siteBceiling@siteBflat: term 1 is 1 when site A assigns the constant, term 2 is 1 if `confidence = winner.score` ever returns to that arm (it must stay 0), term 3 is 1 when site B wraps the constant in the monotone-downward Math.min ceiling, term 4 counts BARE `confidence: RERANK_DECLINED_CONFIDENCE,` assignments in gather-candidates.ts and MUST stay 0 -- that is the regression this claim exists to catch. NOTE the mapper file holds a THIRD `confidence = winner.score` in the fallback_simplified arm at `winner = fallbackCandidate` -- that one is CORRECT and deliberately out of scope, because its score is `fbr.confidence * 0.85`, an already-scaled confidence rather than a retrieval score. A bare file-wide grep for `confidence = winner.score` therefore cannot express this claim, which is why the command isolates site A's block. Standard caveat: a `backend` claim greps a CHECKED-OUT tree, not master and not the box's built .next. EXTENDED 2026-08-07: the confidence_gate_backstop leg itself now takes the constant as a CEILING too -- `confidence = Math.min(RERANK_DECLINED_CONFIDENCE, gateResult.confidence)` in mapIngredientWithFallback() -- closing the last unbounded read (the exact-name assessConfidence 1.0 from high_confidence_clear_winner, which cannot be capped at the producer because the agreement lift legitimately consumes it; T5 in confidence-gate.test.ts pins that producer on purpose). Term 5 is 1 when the backstop ceiling is present. Term 6 counts the hand-transcribed mirror in scripts/eval/winner-diff.ts's replaySelection() backstop arm -- the two halves of the same edit drift apart unless both are present, which is the standing hazard of anchor-bounded transcription and exactly how #256's first cut mismeasured its own PR.
claims.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const s=fs.readFileSync('src/lib/mapping/map-ingredient-with-fallback.ts','utf8');const m=s.match(/const MIN_FALLBACK_RAW_SCORE[\s\S]{0,1200}?selectionReason = 'scored_by_confidence';/);const declined=m&&/confidence = RERANK_DECLINED_CONFIDENCE;/.test(m[0])?1:0;const raw=m&&/confidence = winner\.score;/.test(m[0])?1:0;const g=fs.readFileSync('src/lib/mapping/gather-candidates.ts','utf8');const ceil=(g.match(/confidence: Math\.min\(RERANK_DECLINED_CONFIDENCE, Math\.max\(0, Math\.min\(1, top1\.score\)\)\),/g)||[]).length;const flat=(g.match(/confidence: RERANK_DECLINED_CONFIDENCE,/g)||[]).length;const backstop=(s.match(/confidence = Math\\.min\\(RERANK_DECLINED_CONFIDENCE, gateResult\\.confidence\\);/g)||[]).length;const w=fs.readFileSync('scripts/eval/winner-diff.ts','utf8');const mirror=(w.match(/Math\\.min\\(RERANK_DECLINED_CONFIDENCE, backstop\\.confidence\\)/g)||[]).length;process.stdout.write(declined+'@'+raw+'@'+ceil+'@'+flat+'@'+backstop+'@'+mirror)"

claims.claim: OFF records that carry any serving row carry EXACTLY ONE of them, and that is the load-bearing fact behind the 2026-08-09 decision NOT to build serving-class cache keys. Measured 2026-08-09: of 770,995 OffFood barcodes with an OffServing row, 770,902 have exactly one and only 93 have two or more (n=2 -> 42, n=3 -> 13, n=4 -> 37, n=5 -> 1), i.e. 0.012%. Contrast FatSecretFood, where 20,616 of 24,123 (85.5%) carry >=2 and ZERO carry none. That separation is why 'prefer the candidate carrying the requested unit' is not a per-record ranking feature at all but a LANE PREFERENCE in disguise (OFF is 3,550 of the 4,702 cached identities), which re-opens plan item #18 and collides with the cross_source_margin save gate. If an OFF ingest ever starts delivering genuinely multi-descriptor records, the ranking half of that decision must be re-adjudicated: there would finally be something to select over. This claim is deliberately a THRESHOLD, not a count, so ordinary ingest drift does not red it and a structural change does: it emits 1 while >=2-descriptor OFF records stay under 1% of OFF records with any serving row. It says NOTHING about whether the descriptors are good; OffServing is ~8.7% pure restatements of the per-100g basis ('100g', '1 portion (100 g)'), so the real per-unit choice inside the OFF lane is smaller than even 0.012% suggests.
claims.command: docker exec mealspire-db psql -U postgres -d mealspire -At -c "SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT barcode FROM \"OffServing\" GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*)>=2) t) * 100.0 / GREATEST((SELECT count(DISTINCT barcode) FROM \"OffServing\"),1) < 1.0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END"

claims.claim: A nutrition modifier (sugar free / fat free / low sodium / diet / unsweetened) can be dropped from `normalizedName` before retrieval, and this claim pins the four code facts that decide where the fix must go. Measured 2026-08-10 by A/B on the injected string alone, same rawText, same build WFq5Sm-42xjvhD2N6mbel: normalizedForm 'bbq sauce' -> off_0665591893051 at 36 g / 90 kcal / 22 g sugar (panel 250 kcal, 61.11 g sugar per 100 g) versus 'sugar free bbq sauce' -> off_0628251683140 Firebarns Sugar Free BBQ Sauce at 30 g / 15 kcal / 2 g sugar. 6.0x kcal, 11x sugar, so a COMPLIANT STRING FIXES THE BILL and the string is the whole defect. The four output terms are ordered@segPrep@segDiet@idDiet. Term 1 is 1 while ai-normalize.ts's prompt ORDERS this exact preservation ('MUST PRESERVE nutrition-affecting modifiers in BOTH normalized_name AND canonical_base', with "sugar free pudding" as a worked example) -- it is load-bearing because the drops happen ANYWAY, which is the measured evidence that a prompt is a request and not a mechanism; if that rule is ever deleted the argument for siting the fix in code loses its precedent and this doc must be re-reasoned. Term 2 is 1 while SEGMENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT in ai-segmenter.ts names prep modifiers as its keep-class. Terms 3 and 4 are TRIPWIRES THAT MUST STAY 0 UNTIL THE FIX SHIPS, and are expected to flip to 1 when it does: term 3 goes 1 when the segmenter prompt starts naming diet/nutrition modifiers, term 4 goes 1 when IDENTITY_QUALIFIERS (today exactly {cooked, whole, raw, dried, canned}) gains a diet member. A red on 3 or 4 therefore means 'the fix landed, re-date the owner doc', not 'the code regressed'.
